plan_preamble: The goal is a small standard-library-only arithmetic helper: `add(a, b)` in `arithmetic.py` at the repository root returns `a + b`. The repository currently contains only `feature.md` and orchestrator artifacts under `feature/`, with no existing Python code, packages, or test setup, so the module and tests are created from scratch. The public signature is positional `add(a, b)` with no defaults or extra parameters, and it must not be changed by later tasks. Tests use `unittest` in a single root-level file, `test_arithmetic.py`, so `python -m unittest` discovers them without any configuration. Tasks that edit the test file run in sequence to avoid write conflicts.

tasks.title: Implement add function in arithmetic module
tasks.description: Create `arithmetic.py` at the repository root containing `def add(a, b):` that returns `a + b`, with no default arguments and no extra public names. Use only the Python standard library; the module needs no imports at all. Interface contract: `arithmetic.add(a, b)` is the public API consumed by the test tasks T002-T004, and its signature must not change afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: `arithmetic.py` exists at the repository root and defines `def add(a, b):` with exactly two positional parameters and no defaults
`grep -n import arithmetic.py` shows no imports, or only standard-library imports

tasks.title: Add unittest for positive operands
tasks.description: Create `test_arithmetic.py` at the repository root with `import unittest` and `from arithmetic import add`, plus a `unittest.TestCase` subclass (for example `TestAddPositive`) containing at least one test that asserts `add(1, 2) == 3` and `add(10, 20) == 30`. Do not add negative or zero cases yet; T003 and T004 extend this same file. Add an `if __name__ == '__main__': unittest.main()` guard.
acceptance_criteria: `test_arithmetic.py` exists at the repository root and imports `add` from `arithmetic`
`python -m unittest test_arithmetic.TestAddPositive` runs at least one test and reports `OK`
The test file contains no assertions involving negative numbers or zero operands

tasks.title: Add unittest for negative operands
tasks.description: Extend `test_arithmetic.py` with a `unittest.TestCase` subclass (for example `TestAddNegative`) that asserts `add(-1, -2) == -3`, `add(-5, 3) == -2`, and `add(5, -3) == 2`. Keep the existing `TestAddPositive` class from T002 unchanged. Only edit `test_arithmetic.py`; `arithmetic.py` must not change.
acceptance_criteria: `test_arithmetic.py` contains a class with assertions for `add(-1, -2)`, `add(-5, 3)`, and `add(5, -3)` with the expected results `-3`, `-2`, and `2`
`arithmetic.py` is unchanged compared with the T001 version, as shown by `git diff --stat -- arithmetic.py` producing no output

tasks.title: Add unittest for zero operands
tasks.description: Extend `test_arithmetic.py` with a `unittest.TestCase` subclass (for example `TestAddZero`) that asserts `add(0, 0) == 0`, `add(0, 7) == 7`, `add(7, 0) == 7`, and `add(0, -4) == -4`. Leave the classes from T002 and T003 unchanged. Only edit `test_arithmetic.py`.
acceptance_criteria: `test_arithmetic.py` contains a class with assertions for `add(0, 0)`, `add(0, 7)`, `add(7, 0)`, and `add(0, -4)` with the expected results `0`, `7`, `7`, and `-4`
The `TestAddPositive` and `TestAddNegative` classes still exist in `test_arithmetic.py` with their original assertions, as shown by `grep -c 'class TestAdd' test_arithmetic.py` printing `3`

tasks.title: Verify the arithmetic test module end to end
tasks.description: Run the full test module from the repository root with `python -m unittest -v test_arithmetic` and confirm that every test class from T002-T004 is discovered and passes. This task makes no file changes. If a failure shows that `add` is wrong, the fix belongs in `arithmetic.py` and is out of scope here, so report it instead of editing. Its only job is to confirm the feature as a whole.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m unittest -v test_arithmetic` exits with status 0 and reports `OK`
The verbose output lists tests from all three classes `TestAddPositive`, `TestAddNegative`, and `TestAddZero`
`git status --porcelain -- arithmetic.py test_arithmetic.py` shows both files as present, with no other changes made by this task
